title: batch window shift bug hypotheses
content:
Quick notes / brain dump — trying to capture breadcrumbs for the throughput regression that started 2026-02-28. This is a personal scratchpad; messy.

Summary (short):
- Observable: end-to-end throughput dropped ~35% on hosted-api route /v1/generate for medium-length prompts. p95 latency up from ~120ms to ~480ms.
- Hypothesis (top): continuous-batcher effective batch_window_ms was reduced (config drift or rollout) causing more small batches and reduced token throughput. Secondary: KV cache miss rate increase exacerbated per-token cost and slowed kernel paths.

What I saw (quick metrics):
- Baseline (2026-02-25): median batch size ~12 tokens/req, mean batch_size 8.6, request rate 250 req/s, tokens/sec ~1.2M. p95 latency 120ms.
- After regression (2026-02-28 03:12 UTC): median batch size ~4, mean 3.7, request rate ~230 req/s, tokens/sec ~760k. p95 latency ~480ms.
- Prometheus counters: inference_batching_batches_total spiked in count but average batch_size decreased. inference_kv_cache_hit_ratio dropped from 0.95 -> 0.61 (on model LlamaX-13b-fp16).

Logs / snippets I grabbed:
- runtime logs (gpu-node-07):
  [2026-02-28T03:11:58Z] INFO  continuous_batcher: batch window expired (id=abcd1234) size=2 window_ms=5 reason=timer
  [2026-02-28T03:12:01Z] WARN  continuous_batcher: small-batch flush heuristic triggered size=1 route=/v1/generate request_id=xyz
  [2026-02-28T03:12:05Z] INFO  kv_cache: miss (seq=1) key=conv-9 dev=nvme1p1

- Admin endpoint dump (quick):
  $ curl -sS http://gpu-node-07:8080/admin/config | jq '.continuous_batching, .batch_window_ms, .max_batch_size'
  true
  5
  256

- Note: batch_window_ms=5 (ms). That stands out — default we use in prod is usually 20-50ms for this workload.

Commands I ran (local):
- check metrics tail: kubectl -n runtime logs -l app=runtime --tail 200 | grep "batch window" -n -A2
- admin readback: curl -sS http://{node}:8080/admin/config | jq '.continuous_batching, .batch_window_ms, .max_latency_ms'
- replay test: python tools/replay_workload.py --trace traces/2026-02-25-medium.json --rate 240 --target gpu-node-07 > replay-out.log 2>&1 &
- quick throughput probe to the vhost: 
  for i in {1..6}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -d '{\"input\": \"hello world\"}' https://hosted-api.redwood.com/v1/generate | jq '.latency'; done

Errors / oddities I noticed: 
- Admin config showed continuous_batching true but window_ms=5. Rolling back to 20ms in staging increases average batch size in replay from 3.8 -> 9.1 and tokens/sec improves ~2.2x.
- KV cache churn: dev/nvme GC logs show frequent small evictions around same time window; eviction count went from ~30/min -> ~450/min. Possible correlation: smaller batches cause more random KV accesses and shorter lived caches.
- A/B rollout note: there was a config change merged in PR 510 that touched the default window for the new experiment. It looks like the change didn't set an env override for prod and the config server used a new smaller default.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) rollout/config drift: batch_window_ms default changed to 5ms (PR 510) -> small batches -> underutilized GPU kernels -> throughput drop.
2) traffic shift to shorter prompts: more short requests reduce aggregation opportunities; but metric shows request length distribution stable across days, so less likely.
3) KV cache invalidation bug: small batches flush KV usage more often or sequence alignment bug causing misses -> slower per-token runs.
4) Scheduler/CPU starvation: host-level load (docker/oom) causing timers to fire early -> effectively shorter realized batch windows. Need to check host load at 03:11 UTC.

Quick experiments to run (ordered):
- Hotfix A: increase batch_window_ms to 30ms on one node pool (canary) and measure realtime: focus on mean batch_size, tokens/sec, p95.
  commands: 
    curl -X PATCH http://config-service:8200/flags/continuous_batching -d '{"batch_window_ms":30}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
    watch -n 5 'kubectl -n runtime exec -it runtime-gpu-07 -- curl -sS localhost:8080/admin/metrics | grep "inference_batch_size" -n'
- Hotfix B: enable forced KV pinning (experimental flag) to check if cache hit ratio recovers.
- Replay test: re-run traces with controlled prompt length (short vs medium vs long) to isolate traffic shape effects. Use replay_workload.py into canary nodes.
- Host-check: collect sar/iostat for the host window and check CPU steal, loadavg.

Instrumentation additions to add (ops tickets):
- Emit continuous_batcher.window_observed_ms histogram (we currently only emit config as single value). We need distribution of observed windows to detect timer jitter.
- Add metric for small_batch_flush_count per-route.
- KV cache eviction reasons in more detail (LRU vs forced) as label.

Notes to self (low level):
- The runtime uses high-watermark flush (max_batch_tokens) and timer flush (batch_window_ms). Timer flush at 5ms basically beats the aggregation for our median inter-arrival. If timers fire too aggressively, we get tiny batches and GPU kernel launch overhead dominates.
- There is a code path: if continuous_batching and (route_throughput < threshold) then reduce window for latency SLOs — check whether this logic was inverted by PR 510 (looking at collapse of threshold check).

Breadcrumb timeline (rough):
- 2026-02-27 22:12 UTC: PR 510 merged to runtime defaults (update continuous batching defaults).
- 2026-02-28 03:07 UTC: first alert: p95 latency > 200ms on hosted-api.
- 2026-02-28 03:10 UTC: small-batch flush logs appear across gpu-node-07 and gpu-node-09.
- 2026-02-28 03:20 UTC: rollback attempted in canary (staged to staging only).

Immediate next steps (what I'll do):
- 09:00: spin a canary with batch_window_ms=30ms on pool 'realtime-canary'. Run replay traces and compare tokens/sec. (ping Lina for canary infra)
- Open quick PR to set production flag override to 30ms while we investigate PR 510 semantics. (I can cut this today)
- Add a Prometheus query to the runbook dashboard showing observed batch_window_ms, avg_batch_size, kv_cache_hit_ratio over the last 72h.

If this is config drift, mitigation is trivial (override to previous defaults). If it's host-level timer jitter or CPU starvation, we need SRE help to dig host metrics. If it's KV cache regression, open a separate bug with reproducer and add more detailed KV labels.

Misc notes / random thoughts:
- Could also be an interaction with new autobalance routing: if requests are now more evenly spread across more nodes, per-node input rate drops -> batch sizes drop. Check routing table changes on 2026-02-27.
- If we push window up too far we risk latency SLO violations for tail customers; need to run p99 checks on canary.

TODO (short):
- [ ] Canary change: batch_window_ms -> 30ms (realtime-canary)
- [ ] Replay: short/medium/long traces against canary and baseline
- [ ] Add window_observed_ms histogram metric (instrumentation ticket)
- [ ] Check config-server rollout logs for PR 510 (who/what/when)
- [ ] Confirm KV eviction reason labels for nvme pools

End of dump. Will tidy into a confluence note if we find root cause.

-- Ravi
